tldr: AgentRouter is a knowledge-graph-guided framework that formulates multi-agent QA as a routing problem, using a heterogeneous GNN trained on empirical performance signals to learn adaptive collaboration schemes across diverse agents and LLM backbones.
contributions: KG-based formulation of multi-agent QA: first framework converting multi-agent question answering into knowledge graphs where nodes represent queries, agent prompts, fine-grained entities, and contextual interactions
Graph-supervised collaboration learning: learns adaptive collaboration schemes using supervised graph signals instead of LLM-based judges or heuristic ensembling
Robust empirical validation: consistently outperforms best single agent and SOTA baselines across benchmarks and LLM backbones
methods: The authors convert each QA instance (query + context) into a knowledge graph containing query nodes, entity nodes (extracted via spaCy for named entities, temporal expressions, and numerical mentions), and agent nodes (each representing a backbone LLM plus prompting strategy). Edges encode lexical query-entity links, dependency-parse entity-entity relations, agent-identified relevant entities, and trainable query-agent routing connections. A heterogeneous GNN (RouterGNN) performs type-aware message passing across node types with learned gates per edge type. Supervision is derived from temperature-scaled softmax over empirical F1 scores of all candidate agents, minimizing KL divergence. Final predictions use weighted aggregation (e.g., weighted voting) of agent outputs based on learned routing distributions.
results: AgentRouter consistently outperforms single-agent, ensemble baselines, and SOTA routing methods (LLM-Blender, HybridLLM, GraphRouter) across four benchmarks: HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, NewsQA, and TriviaQA. Gains are especially pronounced on multi-hop datasets. Restricting to top-K agents (K=3, 5, 10) sometimes exceeds the full unrestricted ensemble, with moderate K (around 5-10) working best on multi-hop tasks. A substantial gap to the Oracle (theoretical upper bound using the best agent per question) remains. Performance generalizes across four backbones: Llama-3-8b-instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Turbo, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1, and gpt-oss-20b.
limitations: Substantial gap remains between AgentRouter and Oracle (the theoretical upper bound of always selecting the best agent)
Top-K clipping behavior varies by task type: helps multi-hop reasoning but single-hop QA benefits from more agents, suggesting inconsistent behavior across QA paradigms
Evaluated on only four QA benchmarks and four LLM backbones, limiting generalization claims
Performance differences across RouterGNN hyperparameter configurations (layers, hidden dimensions) were modest but the analysis was truncated in the provided text
